title: ARP 解析：同网段广播请求、跨网段问网关
expected_output:
=== ARP: same-subnet resolution ===
  A ARP REQUEST (broadcast ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff): who has 192.168.1.20? tell 192.168.1.10
  B ARP REPLY (UNICAST to AA:AA:AA:AA:AA:AA): 192.168.1.20 is at BB:BB:BB:BB:BB:BB
  A cache after reply: {'192.168.1.10': 'AA:AA:AA:AA:AA:AA'}
  request = broadcast, reply = unicast

=== ARP: CROSS-subnet resolution ===
  A wants 10.2.3.4 which is NOT in 192.168.1.0/24
  step 1: A checks its own subnet mask -> destination is off-subnet
  step 2: A sends the packet to its GATEWAY 192.168.1.1
  step 3: A resolves the GATEWAY's MAC (NOT the final host's MAC)
  -> frame: dst MAC = 11:11:11:11:11:11 (gateway), dst IP = 10.2.3.4 (final host)
  routers do NOT forward ARP: ARP only works inside one broadcast domain

=== gratuitous ARP ===
  host boots -> broadcasts 'who has MY-OWN-IP?'
  if someone answers -> IP CONFLICT detected
  if nobody answers  -> everyone updates their cache (fast failover)
code:
print("=== ARP: same-subnet resolution ===")

class Host:
    def __init__(self, name, ip, mac):
        self.name, self.ip, self.mac = name, ip, mac
        self.cache = {}
        self.received = []
    def who_has(self, target_ip, broadcast_to):
        print(f"  {self.name} ARP REQUEST (broadcast ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff): who has {target_ip}? tell {self.ip}")
        for h in broadcast_to:
            h.received.append((self.name, target_ip, self.ip, self.mac))
    def handle(self, asker_name, target_ip, asker_ip, asker_mac):
        if self.ip == target_ip:
            print(f"  {self.name} ARP REPLY (UNICAST to {asker_mac}): {self.ip} is at {self.mac}")
            return (asker_ip, asker_mac)
        return None

a = Host("A", "192.168.1.10", "AA:AA:AA:AA:AA:AA")
b = Host("B", "192.168.1.20", "BB:BB:BB:BB:BB:BB")
gw = Host("GW", "192.168.1.1", "11:11:11:11:11:11")
lan = [b, gw]

a.who_has("192.168.1.20", lan)
for h in lan:
    for ev in h.received:
        r = h.handle(*ev)
        if r:
            a.cache[r[0]] = r[1]
print(f"  A cache after reply: {a.cache}")
print("  request = broadcast, reply = unicast")
print()

print("=== ARP: CROSS-subnet resolution ===")
print("  A wants 10.2.3.4 which is NOT in 192.168.1.0/24")
print("  step 1: A checks its own subnet mask -> destination is off-subnet")
print("  step 2: A sends the packet to its GATEWAY 192.168.1.1")
print("  step 3: A resolves the GATEWAY's MAC (NOT the final host's MAC)")
print(f"  -> frame: dst MAC = {gw.mac} (gateway), dst IP = 10.2.3.4 (final host)")
print("  routers do NOT forward ARP: ARP only works inside one broadcast domain")
print()
print("=== gratuitous ARP ===")
print("  host boots -> broadcasts 'who has MY-OWN-IP?'")
print("  if someone answers -> IP CONFLICT detected")
print("  if nobody answers  -> everyone updates their cache (fast failover)")
